title: Four GBM detectors and Konus-Wind records support two late pulses of GRB 190419A
abstract: We test the long GBM structure of GRB 190419A, which remained open in an earlier campaign study. Four selected NaI detectors show pulses at 155-175 s and 200-220 s after the trigger. Both pulses remain positive in every detector under five smooth background fits. Combined count scores range from 11.9 to 26.9 for the first late pulse and 22.6 to 36.6 for the second. Their total net counts are 1.04-1.17 times those in the first 20 s. Independent Konus-Wind pages and plots from 2019 record both late episodes. This supports separated emission across more than 200 s, rather than a smooth GBM background error alone. It does not establish exact photon durations or an engine mechanism. The windows were selected after inspection. Source response, structured backgrounds and exact sky association were not fitted. Konus-Wind source retrieval used HTTP after HTTPS failed, which limits that check. This is a check of known pulses, not a new discovery. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and retrieval steps are included. External raw and record-level files remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Net count rates from four GBM detectors after separate linear background fits. Orange bands mark the three tested intervals.

citations.reason: We test its unresolved long structure for GRB 190419A with CTIME counts and independent Konus-Wind records. No prior code or derived values are reused.
